summary: Keep an unpublished reserved release at its approved version when Release Please runs in manifest mode.
userImpact: Replacing an unpublished candidate regenerates the approved version instead of proposing an extra minor release.

instructions: Use explicit replacement preparation after the corrected protected-main helper is merged.

configuration: The preparation helper applies a managed Release-As commit override to the newest reviewed first-party code PR contained in the source. The pinned action ignores its release-as input in manifest mode.
Only labels actually attached to the old reservation are removed; missing legacy label definitions are tolerated.

notes: No application, database or published-package change.

security: Replacement still requires an explicit protected-main dispatch and verified absence of both semantic tag and GitHub release. Publication and all candidate acceptance gates remain separate.
Generated release PR bodies and existing human commit overrides are not rewritten by the preparation helper.
documentation: The artifact-promotion runbook explains managed version directives, published-baseline behavior and idempotent label reconciliation.
knownLimitations: Only unpublished reserved versions may be replaced. The replacement still needs generated-document agreement and exact signed candidate acceptance.
rollback: Stop replacement dispatches and revert the preparation helper if required. Retain existing releases and signed records; no database or package rollback is needed.
validation: 39 local record, observer, recovery, workflow and replacement-metadata regressions passed, including first-party ancestry, review preservation, idempotent version directives, missing legacy labels and rejected human overrides.

The actual pinned release-please 17.6.0 parser and version strategy recognize the managed code-PR override and retain 0.30.0 even when the manifest already reserves 0.30.0; the local proof performs no publication.
